profile.reading:
Switch Las Vegas 7 sits at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard, Las Vegas, Nevada, in unincorporated Enterprise, Clark County. Data center industry aggregators place its opening year at 2008, and Switch's own February 2014 press release for the neighboring SUPERNAP 8 building describes Las Vegas 7 as "the original SUPERNAP," sitting several hundred yards away, corroborating that this building was the founding structure of what became Switch's sprawling Core Campus. Switch does not publish individual square footage, megawatt capacity, or redundancy-design figures for Las Vegas 7 on its current site; its historical role as the company's first purpose-built Las Vegas data center, from which the campus later expanded to include Las Vegas 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 14 among numbered buildings, is documented only indirectly through Switch's references to it in later press releases about newer buildings. Switch was founded by Rob Roy, who in 2002 acquired a former Enron-affiliated facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically sited over a fiber-optic backbone serving national technology companies; that 2002 acquisition is understood to be the origin of the Core Campus that Las Vegas 7 anchors. Switch's Core Campus is marketed today as offering up to 495 megawatts of power upon completion and 100 percent renewable energy, with Nevada's consumer-use-tax and property-tax abatement program, administered through the Governor's Office of Economic Development, cited by Switch as a business advantage of its home state.

Clark County's data center cluster, anchored substantially by Switch's Core Campus that Las Vegas 7 helped originate, has helped establish Las Vegas as a significant secondary U.S. data center market outside the major coastal and Northern Virginia hubs. Switch has since built a large solar and battery-storage generation program, including the Switch Station 1 and Switch Station 2 projects and the more recent Gigawatt Nevada development, to support its stated 100 percent renewable energy claim across its Nevada campuses, a program that traces its roots to the original site Las Vegas 7 anchors.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Switch Las Vegas 7, is part of Switch Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, spanning locations including Las Vegas, Enterprise, and near McCarran. Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as CEO and chief engineer, and the company is headquartered in Las Vegas. Wikipedia coverage states that in 2002 Roy acquired a former Enron facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, which became the foundation of the Las Vegas Core Campus. That campus has grown to eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to reach 2.3 million square feet across 12 buildings. Switch also operates the Citadel Campus in Storey County in Northern Nevada, a separate 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development announced in January 2015, and a Grand Rapids, Michigan Pyramid Campus, but those are distinct from this Las Vegas registry cluster. In December 2022 DigitalBridge and IFM Investors completed an 11 billion dollar acquisition, taking Switch private. Data center industry directories place Switch Las Vegas 7 at 7135 S Decatur Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV. Sourced from datacenterHawk, a second directory (Baxtel) lists the same address for this building though that same directorys table repeats this address for several other unrelated Switch buildings, suggesting a template default there rather than an independent confirmation, so this is treated as effectively single-source.  Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. This registry rows address, where given below, therefore comes from data center industry aggregator directories, leads-only sources per this projects source hierarchy, not confirmed directly by the operator.

Switch Las Vegas 7 is one of eleven buildings in the Switch Las Vegas Core Campus, a facility cluster that began with a former Enron site acquired in 2002 and now spans over 2 million square feet. The operator publishes no power or capacity figure for this specific building, and no IT load, rack count, or accelerator density. Without published specifications, this building's relevance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from operator data.

In Nevada, 26 data center facilities are mapped in public records, but only 2 publish power figures to the operator's specification page. This facility ranks third in the state by published megawatts, yet the state context lists only 10.37 MW of published capacity across all Nevada facilities with disclosed figures, a figure that reflects the scarcity of public capacity disclosure statewide rather than absolute scale. The operator's own locations page confirms no street addresses, power ratings, or building-specific specifications are published for any of its five exascale campuses.

To determine whether this campus matters to AI, readers require published power draw, IT load density, or nameplate capacity. The operator does not provide these figures. The research status for this entry is complete, meaning no published specification exists to retrieve.
